articles.title: Anger at Tuchel over World Cup exit exposes biggest obstacle to England success | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: Manager is not responsible for underlying weaknesses but there are reasons for optimism in the buildup to Euro 2028. In the end, Steve, Brian, Gaz or similar, he’s just not done the job he was hired to do. The job? The one he was hired to do? He’s not done it. How can I put this?
body: How many times have you heard variations on this statement in the few short, tender weeks since England’s World Cup campaign? Perhaps you strayed too close to a sport-themed radio show, or accidentally ingested a celebrity football pundit podcast. Either way the verdict is pretty much universal, and delivered always with an air of finality, a sad shake of the head.

The non-winning of a World Cup. The failure to make substitutions to nullify big-game full-bore Lionel Messi. The non-doing of a job you were, apparently, hired for. Even if that job, in isolation, was also a pretty stupid idea in the first place.

Tuchel made a decent effort last week at steering attention to the more favourable aspects of England’s World Cup, but it’s clear he’s fighting a losing battle here. Nobody cares about his all-time highest managerial win ratio, or a best-ever England World Cup performance overseas.
points: Manager is not responsible for underlying weaknesses but there are reasons for optimism in the buildup to Euro 2028.
In the end, Steve, Brian, Gaz or similar, he’s just not done the job he was hired to do.

articles.title: Leeds and Warrington tussle for Grand Final spot
articles.summary: Ahead of the their Super League play-off semi-final, Leeds Rhinos and Warrington Wolves are aiming to assert themselves back at rugby league's top table.
body: Off the back of a bye week courtesy of their second-placed finish, Leeds welcome Warrington on Friday for the first of two play-off semi-finals.

But with St Helens, Wigan and Hull KR taking it in turns to dominate the domestic stage over the best part of the past decade, can two of the titans of the game muscle in on the party and seal the first spot in 3 October's Super League Grand Final?
Leeds come into the fixture following two losses against Wigan and Hull FC at home.
Looking further back, they closed out their regular campaign with three defeats in five matches.

articles.title: ‘It’s not in us’: Anthony Gordon backs Tuchel over England’s possession problem
articles.summary: Barcelona winger says England cannot play like Spain. Gordon: players ‘could have done more’ in semi-final. Anthony Gordon has sided with Thomas Tuchel’s assertion that controlling games through possession is not part of English football’s DNA.
body: England’s perennial struggle to keep the ball when under pressure flared when a place in the final was within touching distance in July, allowing Argentina to fight back and go through with two late goals. The pain has not gone away and there has been intense scrutiny of Tuchel’s role in Atlanta. The head coach’s tactical choices were criticised and he faced a backlash after saying “ball possession” was not in his team’s DNA.

But Gordon, who thinks he will always be scarred by losing against Argentina, sided with Tuchel’s observations about England’s style as he looked towards the Nations League game against Spain on Saturday. The 25-year-old admitted the side had an ingrained inability to control games but argued they should stop trying to copy other nations.
Gordon has gained an insight into the Spanish understanding of how to use the ball since his move to Barcelona. His view is that England should lean more into their physical strengths.

articles.title: Tasmania Devils line up female voice to sing team song in AFL first
articles.summary: Expansion club wants official new recording to be inclusive. Selection panel will deliberate before choosing song by end of year. Kylie Minogue will dazzle 100,000 fans at the MCG this weekend, but the Tasmania Devils hope there will soon be another female vocal heard on grand final day.
body: In what would be an AFL first, the club wants to have both female and male voices on the official recording of their team song, which is expected to be selected by the end of the year.

The Devils’ song selection panel also wants the melody to sound just as good whether it is sung by an AFL player, one from the AFLW or any supporter in the stands, and that the lyrics are inclusive of all Tasmanians.
Chief executive from the Tasmanian Symphony Orchestra, Caroline Sharpen, is part of the eight-person panel which has met three times to begin developing criteria, due to be released next month.
“One of the things that struck me in one of the very early meetings was just hearing how important it is for the team song to carry a female voice as well,” she said.

articles.title: Man Utd selling Old Trafford turf cubes for £125
articles.summary: Manchester United is selling pieces of its Old Trafford pitch for £125 each, an initiative announced the same day the club reported its overall debt remains more than £1bn.
body: Manchester United are selling pieces of their Old Trafford pitch for £125 each.
The initiative was announced the same day that the club reported that overall debt remains more than £1bn.
While United recorded a record revenue of £677.6m and a £22.6m operating profit for 2025-26, they had a pre-tax loss of £43m.
The 13-time Premier League champions also confirmed £63.5m had been spent on buying land for the team's new stadium, which is expected to cost more than £2bn overall.

articles.title: Charles taking record-breaking price tag in his stride
articles.summary: Fulham midfielder Shea Charles tells BBC Sport NI he does "not really think about" the price tag which saw him become Northern Ireland's most expensive footballer when he joined Premier League Fulham from Southampton.
body: If Shea Charles is feeling a weight of expectation from being the most expensive Northern Ireland footballer ever his demeanour does not betray it.

Interviewed by BBC Sport NI before the forthcoming four-game Nations League bonanza, the Fulham midfielder cuts a laid-back but determined figure who is keen to play a key part in helping a young Northern Ireland side continue to build on recent progress.
Charles' record-breaking £30m move from Championship side Southampton to the Cottagers in the summer gave him the opportunity to move up a division and ply his trade in the Premier League.

"I think I was like second or third before that. But to be number one, it's really cool. Just to be in the Premier League and just being able to play my football is amazing," he told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

articles.title: Why this break has come at the worst time for De Zerbi & Spurs
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains the different factors that mean Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi needs time with his players to build a proper team.
body: Big spending always means big ambitions, but shelling out so much money on so many players the way Tottenham did this summer produces problems for any manager, and there is no quick fix.

If I was given a bundle of cash and asked to buy an outfit for a wedding, and I spent every penny of it on pink shoes, brown trousers, yellow shirt and orange tie, then I am sure you would all say that just doesn't work.
That is similar to what has happened at Spurs, where the board backed Roberto de Zerbi to the hilt with an outlay on new players of around £400m.

It was an almost unprecedented occurrence from a club that has always been renowned for being careful with investment in their team, and it sent expectations from many Spurs supporters through the roof.

articles.title: “They were paying 120”: Ex-PL boss reveals details of Man United’s failed bid for football legend
articles.summary: 1. Former Tottenham Hotspur boss Andre Villas-Boas has revealed the extreme lengths Manchester United were willing to go to in order to sign Gareth Bale before he eventually chose to join Real Madrid. Failed pursuit.
body: Following the retirement of the iconic Sir Alex Ferguson, United set about rebuilding the team and had identified Bale as a top target.
Bale was coming off a stellar season with Tottenham Hotspur in which he plundered 26 goals.

His spell at White Hart Lane brought a glittering haul: PFA Player of the Year in 2011 and 2013, a clean sweep of PFA Player, PFA Young Player and Football Writers’ Footballer of the Year in 2013, and three consecutive PFA Team of the Year selections between 2010 and 2013.
United, under David Moyes, made a strong push for Bale, but he opted to join Real Madrid for a then-world-record transfer fee of €100 million.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz says he ‘misses’ rival Jannik Sinner
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has said he “misses” his biggest rival, Jannik Sinner, with the Italian currently sidelined with a knee injury. After splitting the four grand slams of 2025 between them many expected the pair to be equally dominant in 2026.
body: Spaniard Alcaraz missed nearly five months of the season with a wrist injury before returning to defend his title at the US Open, where he lost in the quarter-finals, while Sinner has been out of action since Wimbledon with the knee problem.

Alcaraz will play for the first time since his US Open exit at the exhibition Laver Cup in London this week, after saying that he would be more conservative in his playing schedule in order to manage his physical health.
He told BBC Sport ahead of the competition: “I have texted him [Sinner] not too much, but a few times when he has been winning everything, mostly at the beginning of the year.
“I miss him, I miss seeing him around, playing against him. He pushes me to be a better player.

articles.title: 'We have our own strengths' – Gordon backs Tuchel’s DNA comments
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon has backed Thomas Tuchel's view that England's players have an inbuilt inability to control matches with possession - and has urged the team to embrace the country's traditional strengths.
body: Tuchel was criticised for England's defensive retreat after Gordon's goal gave them the lead against Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals, an approach which ultimately allowed their rivals to turn the match around in the final stages.

Tuchel responded by hitting out at the 'DNA' of English players. "I think ball possession plays a crucial role; it's maybe not in our DNA like it is in Spanish DNA or in Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball," he said.

Tuchel made those comments despite leaving some of England's most technical players - Cole Palmer, Phil Foden, Trent Alexander-Arnold - out of his World Cup squad, and not giving midfielder Kobbie Mainoo a minute of game time during the tournament.
However, speaking ahead of England's Nations League opener with world champions Spain, Gordon has backed his manager's view.

articles.title: Bills legend Fred Jackson's son follows father's football footsteps
articles.summary: Fred Jackson's son Braeden rushed for 125 yards and scored twice in his breakout game after following an unlikely path reminiscent of his father's.
body: Fred Jackson was back in Buffalo last week wearing a familiar number.

The former Buffalo Bills running back, who became a fan favorite during nine seasons with the Bills, was supporting his son Braeden while touring the new Highmark Stadium with former teammate Marshawn Lynch. Jackson wore an Iowa hoodie with "Jackson 22" across the back.
Two days later, Braeden Jackson gave Bills fans another No. 22 to root for.

The 20-year-old Iowa running back rushed for 125 yards and scored the first two touchdowns of his college career Saturday in a 55-0 victory over Northern Iowa, delivering the first breakout performance of a career beginning to look a little like his father's.

articles.title: Kaptein scores winner as Chelsea earn narrow victory over Austria Wien
articles.summary: Wieke Kaptein scored a stunning goal but Chelsea were given a stern test by Austria Wien as they began their Women's Champions League campaign with a hard-fought 1-0 win at Plough Lane.
body: Chelsea went ahead in spectacular style early on. Sandy Baltimore's run was ended by a well-timed sliding tackle and the ball spun loose. Collecting it 25 yards from goal was Kaptein, and after taking a touch she hammered it in off the bar.
Keira Walsh was forced off injured after 20 minutes, a potential blow for Chelsea ahead of Sunday's WSL game at home to Arsenal.

The home side were living dangerously when goalkeeper Livia Peng fumbled a shot from a short corner routine, palming the ball back out into danger from where Virginia Kirchberger hoisted it over the bar.
There was almost a sublime equaliser when Louise Schoffel danced her way through Chelsea's defence and hit a low shot that flashed inches wide of the post.

articles.title: Does Littler need to change approach to hostile crowds?
articles.summary: Following Luke Littler's latest run-in with a hostile crowd over the weekend, the Sky Sports Love The Darts Podcast has debated whether it is time for the world champion to change his approach.
body: Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the action was overshadowed by the Brit's unhappiness at being repeatedly whistled at by the Dutch crowd.

After facing significant hostility during his win over home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday, Littler threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his victory over Nathan Aspinall on Saturday, prompting referee Charlie Corstorphine to intervene.
Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

On the latest episode of the Love The Darts Podcast, World Series of Darts Finals champion Ross Smith explained his own approach to hostile crowds, which he admits is inspired by three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen.
